display: Teaching assistant at a Levenshulme primary school, single mum, studying part-time with the Open University. I bake, I'm good with kids, and I rarely ask for help.

signals.text: I'm running a cake sale for Theo's under-10s football team today, and we're still about £170 short of new kit.
I have a 2,500-word Open University essay on inclusive practice due 14 October. I have a plan and about 900 words, and I need to turn the plan into an argument.
I'm behind on my degree and juggling it around school hours and Theo's evenings, so I'm short on time and sleep.
I promised thirty cupcakes for the school fair and my lemon drizzle trial batch burnt on the bottom.
The boiler in our flat has been broken for seven weeks and we're boiling kettles for baths.
The landlord's agent stopped replying after my third polite email and has read my chasing message without answering.
There is black mould spreading on the wall in Theo's bedroom. I've moved his bed and run a dehumidifier, but it's still there.
I'd like to find out what my options are for getting repairs done quietly, without turning it into a fight with the agent.
Theo's inhaler use has roughly doubled since last month, and his cough is worse at night when he's at home.
I'm scared that pushing harder on the damp will get us a no-fault eviction notice, and I can't afford to move.
Money is very tight: £1,150 a month take-home against £780 rent, and even a £7.40 launderette trip counts.
I feel I can't ask anyone for help because it would look like I'm failing.

offers.text: Six years as a Key Stage 2 teaching assistant: classroom support, behaviour, reading help, and day-to-day work with children with additional needs.
Paediatric first aid certificate and a calm head in a crisis with children.
Sourdough and celebration cakes. I bake birthday cakes for the class and can do fundraising bakes.
Knowledge of the local parents' WhatsApp groups and the church hall volunteers in Levenshulme, which helps with getting word out about a community event.
Experience fitting part-time Open University study around a job and parenting, including how to plan an essay and use tutor feedback. I can pass on what works.
A parent's view of a school and a football team, so I can give practical help to other parents running small fundraisers.

catchers.hypo: I work for a tenants' advice service in Greater Manchester. I help renters get broken boilers and damp fixed, and I can explain how to do it without putting the tenancy at risk. Would a free chat help you?
catchers.can: Claire could use a confidential conversation about her rights and a safe way to get repairs done quietly. She would pass on the facts: seven weeks without a boiler, an unresponsive agent, and mould.
catchers.confirm: Can you give advice on housing repairs and protection from retaliatory eviction that works for someone who must not risk losing their tenancy?

catchers.hypo: I'm an environmental health officer. If a tenant tells me about damp and mould affecting a child's health, I can explain what the council can do and how a complaint stays confidential. Would that be useful?
catchers.can: Claire could learn what the council can do about the damp and what a complaint would mean for her. Her mum, who wanted her to phone the council, could support her through it.
catchers.confirm: Can you explain, before any complaint is made, how a council complaint about damp works and what protections the tenant has?

catchers.hypo: My child's school keeps telling me they have 'additional needs' and I don't understand what support to ask for. I'd love to talk to someone calm who has worked in classrooms.
catchers.can: Claire can explain in plain language what inclusive support in a primary classroom looks like and what to ask the school for. This also feeds directly into her own OU essay.
catchers.confirm: Is your child at a primary school in England and do you want practical, non-legal guidance on what support to ask for?

catchers.hypo: We're a youth football team run by volunteers and need to raise money for kit. Do you know how to run a simple bake sale or find local sponsors?
catchers.can: Claire can share what she has learned running a cake sale for Theo's team and put the word out through local parents' groups.
catchers.confirm: Are you a grassroots children's team looking to raise a few hundred pounds, rather than a large club?

catchers.hypo: I run a small café or bakery in south Manchester and I'd sponsor a children's football team with a few hundred pounds towards kit in exchange for a mention on the shirts.
catchers.can: Claire can pass this to Theo's coach and the team's parents, which could close the £170 gap on the kit.
catchers.confirm: Are you a local business happy to sponsor an under-10s football team in Manchester?

catchers.hypo: I'm an Open University tutor or study-skills coach, and I can read an essay plan and show how to build an argument from it. Want a second pair of eyes?
catchers.can: Claire could share her 900 words and plan and get feedback on developing the argument before the 14 October deadline.
catchers.confirm: Can you help someone move from a good essay plan to a developed argument in education studies, within about ten days?

catchers.hypo: I'm a parent in Levenshulme with a child who has asthma and a flat with damp. Have you been through this, and what helped?
catchers.can: Claire can talk with another parent who understands living with a child's asthma and damp, and share local contacts. She would reach out through her mum, who is a good listener.
catchers.confirm: Have you personally handled a child's asthma alongside a damp or mould problem in rented housing?

catchers.hypo: I'm worried about a friend who has been served notice after reporting a repair problem. Do you know anyone who understands how that works?
catchers.can: Claire can pass this to Janine, a colleague whose friend went through exactly this, so they can compare what they've learned and find proper support.
catchers.confirm: Is your friend's situation a no-fault eviction notice following a repair complaint in England?

catchers.hypo: I'm a parent who feels I'm failing because I can't ask for help. Does anyone out there get this and just want to talk?
catchers.can: Claire can be a listener for someone who feels they have to cope alone, and she understands how hard asking for help can be.
catchers.confirm: Do you mainly want someone to listen, rather than professional counselling?

forbids.text: I can't do anything that risks my tenancy, including anything that could be read as a hostile act towards the landlord or agent.
I don't want public naming or shaming of the landlord's agent or a confrontation; I prefer to solve things quietly.
I can only take on things outside school hours and Theo's evenings, and not much then.
I can't pay for services at the moment, because money is very tight.
I won't share Theo's health details or photos of his room with anyone who isn't directly helping.

projects.name: Theo's football kit fundraiser
projects.text: New shirts and shorts for the under-10s squad, about £320 in total, with a cake sale at the school fair. We're roughly £170 short and need a bit more help.
roles_needed: parent volunteer to help promote it

policy.t1: When someone shows a real sign they can help, I'll share that our boiler has been broken for seven weeks, the agent isn't replying, and there is mould in Theo's bedroom.
policy.t2: Once trust is established and the person's role is clear, I'll share Theo's increased inhaler use, my fear of an eviction notice, and the money situation.
